identification: Antique bullseye policeman's lantern, 15 cm high (Victorian-style police hand lantern; maker not identified)

entries.note: Hiatt & Co marked Victorian brass bullseye police lantern, UK; Armitage lantern maker unconfirmed. aud_price left blank rather than converting. [AUD 41 converted at GBP 1 = AUD 1.97]

viewing_check: Look for maker's mark (Hiatt & Co etc), belt hook, folding handle, lens intact, darkening shutter working, any police force stamp or Australian provenance.
searches_tried: web: antique bullseye police lantern history; bullseye police lantern Australia sold auction. One UK sale seen. Country Home Antiques page 404.
story: Bullseye lanterns were the Victorian police officer's night tool: a fisheye lens concentrating a candle or oil flame, a belt hook, folding handles and a shutter to darken the light. Collectors identify them by those features, and most are unmarked; Hiatt & Co of Birmingham was a well-known maker. https://heritagearmssa.com/2018/06/26/victorian-police-lanterns/

identification: Three vintage cameras per photos: a folding Vest Pocket Kodak Autographic (c.1914-1920s), an Agfa Parat-I half-frame 35mm (1963), and a Yashica 'EE' rangefinder (model not confirmed) with its manual
viewing_check: Vest Pocket Kodak: bellows pinholes, lens and shutter, autographic scribe door. Yashica: confirm exact model (Electro 35 / EE series) and that the meter and shutter work. Agfa: working shutter, intact lens.
searches_tried: web: Vest Pocket Kodak Autographic history; Agfa Parat-I camera sold price; Kodak VPK sold Leski/Gowans. Only price seen was an old US EBTH sale of a VPK Special in a box (Nov 2017, figure unclear on page) so not recorded. Catawiki Agfa listing gave no usable price. Thriftworld page blocked.
story: The Vest Pocket Kodak was the famous soldiers' camera of WWI; the AWM holds one carried by Sapper Ernest Northey of the 4th Divisional Signal Company, who photographed at Pozieres in 1916 and won the Military Medal. Folding VPKs like this one are a plausible souvenir of that era. The Agfa Parat-I is a 1963 half-frame compact. https://www.awm.gov.au/collection/C1070965

identification: Sharpe Bros stoneware ginger beer bottle/flagon (two-tone cream and brown, wire stopper, label reads 'Sharpe Bros Australia & New Zealand, Original & Largest Hygienic Brewers', stopper date appears 1954), roughly one gallon
viewing_check: Check for chips, cracks and crazing, whether the wire stopper is intact, and stamped marks on the base; condition drives price.
searches_tried: web: Sharpe Bros Swadlincote (wrong firm, UK), Sharpe Bros Australia & New Zealand hygienic brewers; Sharpe Bros stoneware ginger beer sold Australia auction. Carters page (the one comparable) is behind a bot check, skipped. Trade Me result irrelevant. No visible price.
story: Sharpe Brothers were a cordial and ginger beer company founded in Dunedin in 1903 by John Sharpe, who later moved to Australia; they were renowned for ginger beer brewed in gallon stoneware jars and had branches across NSW, Victoria and South Australia until 1972. Note this is not the Derbyshire Sharpe's Pottery of Swadlincote. https://archivescollection.anu.edu.au/index.php/sharpe-brothers

identification: Vintage short fishing rod with turned timber (polished wood) handle, nickel-silver ferrules and a slender flexible tip ('rapier blade' is the catalogue term, probably a fibreglass or solid blade); maker not identified
viewing_check: Look for a maker's name or transfer on the butt or blade, check the tip ring and guides, any cracks or set in the blade; a named maker (Hardy, Allcock, a known Australian maker) would change the value.
searches_tried: web: 'Rapier Blade' fishing rod with Hardy/Allcock/Alvey; rapier blade rod fibreglass Australian 1950s; checked an Australian bamboo fly rod makers page for 'rapier' (no mention). No identification and no price found.
story: I could not identify the maker or find any reference to a 'rapier blade' rod type, so no verified history. Rods with turned timber handles and solid glass or steel blades were common mid-20th century boat and estuary rods.

identification: Three Dinky Toys military models: SRN6 hovercraft in army colours, an armoured tracked vehicle and a field/anti-tank gun
viewing_check: Check for paint chips, missing missiles/parts on the hovercraft, and that the gun elevates and traverses; photo shows gun, tracked vehicle and hovercraft.
searches_tried: WebSearch: 'Dinky Toys Army Hovercraft SRN6 military 290 hovercraft tank cannon'; 'Dinky Toys 290 SRN6 hovercraft sold auction price lot'; 'Dinky Toys 656 88mm gun sold auction lot'. eBay.de ended listings seen (US$60, US$14.99, GBP8.49) do not show sold status so not recorded; Fieldings pages would not load.
story: Dinky's large die-cast SR.N6 hovercraft (no. 290) was made in the 1970s, modelling the Saunders-Roe/British Hovercraft Corporation craft that in 1965 became the first production hovercraft in commercial service, on the Solent between Ryde and Southsea. In military form the real SR.N6 carried up to 55 troops and served with navies from Iran to Brunei. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SR.N6

identification: Vintage small rectangular-tank kerosene lantern/lamp with glass chimney (catalogued as railway lantern), 16 x 15 cm
viewing_check: Look for stamped railway or maker markings (e.g. TGR, VR, NSWGR) on the tank or lid; the photos show a flat oval-ended tin tank with brass filler cap and wick burner.
searches_tried: WebSearch: 'Tasmanian Government Railways lantern railway handlamp history Tasmania sold'. No same-type priced results opened.
story: Not confirmed as railway; Tasmania's railways ran on the Tasmanian Government Railways from 1890s and kerosene hand and signal lamps were standard until electrification. Source for the network: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmanian_Government_Railways (not fetched).

identification: Kriesler brown bakelite mantel radio, state-station and shortwave dial, not tested
viewing_check: Check the model number on the back (likely 11-20 'plum pudding' family), bakelite cracks, and that the dial glass is intact.
searches_tried: WebSearch: 'Kriesler bakelite mantel radio history...'; 'Kriesler 11-20 bakelite radio sold auction lot hammer'. Carters results (bot check) skipped. Brief already holds Gowans results.
story: Kriesler was founded in 1928 by Sydney brothers Alec, Leo and Rae Weingott in Newtown; the name was meant to be Kreisler after the violinist Fritz Kreisler. The rounded bakelite 11-20 earned the nickname 'plum pudding', came in 27 variants, covered broadcast and shortwave and first sold for 18 pounds 19 shillings. Source: https://vk5pas.com/kriesler-11-20a-bakelite.html

viewing_check: Look in the boxes for labelled specimens, especially bright orange-red crocoite (Dundas, Tasmania) and any large polished or cut minerals; photos show shells, crystals and rocks.

Worth a look for labels in these boxes. Source: https://timelineauctions.com/lot/mixed-crystal-and-mineral-specimen-group/257191/

identification: Box and crate of old bottles (types not identified from search)
viewing_check: Look for embossed Tasmanian makers' names (e.g. Cascade, Abbott, Towers, Robertson, Marsden), stoneware ginger beer bottles, Codd/blob-top bottles and pontil marks; photos show two containers of bottles.
searches_tried: WebSearch: 'old Tasmanian bottles collecting Hobart Launceston bottle makers history stoneware ginger beer'; 'lot old bottles crate vintage Tasmanian bottles sold Gowans OR Leski OR Armitage'. No comparable priced results seen.
story: Tasmanian cordial and ginger beer bottles carry the names of local makers: JG Towers opened a machine-equipped Launceston factory in 1850, James Robertson of Hobart became the island's biggest cordial maker by 1872, Cascade ran an aerated water department from 1886 and a Strahan factory for the west coast mines 1899 to 1916, and in 1899 eighteen makers operated across the state. Source: https://utas.edu.au/library/companion_to_tasmanian_history/C/Cordial%20manufacture.htm

identification: Three vintage flat irons including a Chinese sleeve iron (pan iron)
viewing_check: Check the Chinese iron for brass or bronze body and wooden handle, any maker marks, and the other two irons for names or sizes cast into them.
searches_tried: WebSearch: 'Chinese sleeve iron antique pan iron brass history use for silk sleeves sold'; 'Chinese sleeve iron brass wooden handle sold auction lot'. Only retail listings and undated auction results found; no usable price.
story: Chinese pan or silk irons were small metal pans filled with hot coals and used to press silk and sleeves; the SCMP traces Chinese irons back more than 2000 years. Source: https://www.scmp.com/lifestyle/chinese-culture/article/3354357/earliest-chinese-irons-date-back-over-2000-years-heres-how-they-evolved (search result title only, not read).

identification: Mounted wild brown trout skin mount, about 64 cm, on bark slab; likely late 20th century
viewing_check: Check for a taxidermist label or catch date/weight plaque on the back, and fin/tail damage.
searches_tried: WebSearch: Salmon Ponds 1864 brown trout history; mounted taxidermy brown trout bark slab sold auction. Results were UK antique cased trout (Toovey's, Dukes etc.), not comparable and not opened.
story: Brown trout in Australia descend from ova shipped on the clipper Norfolk from London in Jan 1864, hatched at the Salmon Ponds at Plenty, Tasmania on 4 May 1864 (only about 300 of 30,000 surviving ova were trout, added as an afterthought by James Youl). Tasmanian fish were then sent to Victoria, NSW and NZ; Salmon Ponds is the oldest trout hatchery in the Southern Hemisphere. https://tasfish.com/181-trout-fishing/2412-celebrate-the-trout-150-years-in-tasmania-first-born-4-may-1864

identification: Pair of brass bulb-type motor horns (long looped trumpet horns, rubber bulbs missing), early 20th century style
viewing_check: Look for maker's stamps (Lucas, Klaxon, Desmo, etc.), dents or splits in the brass, and whether the reeds are still present.
searches_tried: WebSearch x3: vintage brass bulb car horn sold; early motoring brass horn history; pair brass bulb horns sold auction. Opened Henry Ford museum page (story), a Fieldings lot (redirected to calendar, nothing) and an arteauto listing (page not found). No price recorded.
story: Brass bulb horns like these were the standard warning device on early cars (c. 1900-1915) when cars had to alert pedestrians and horse-drawn traffic; the Henry Ford museum notes the snake-like look was an added incentive to get out of the way. A museum example is a c.1905 British horn, 79 in long. https://www.thehenryford.org/collections/explore/artifact/163156

identification: Decorative timber and brass ship's wheel, 91 cm (36 in), ten turned spokes, brass hub; looks like a modern reproduction rather than a working helm

entries.note: New 36 in teak wall-decor wheel, eight spokes; Armitage wheel is similar size and style, age and wood not confirmed.

viewing_check: Check for a maker's plate or a ship name, evidence of salt-water wear (a real ship's wheel would be heavy and worn), and any cracked rim segments.
searches_tried: WebSearch: 36 inch wooden ship's wheel brass hub price; ship's wheel history. Opened one eBay.de listing for the asking price. Stories from Wikipedia not opened.
story: The spoked wheel replaced the tiller on larger sailing ships in the early 18th century because it gave more leverage; the style is still sold as nautical decor today, and the Armitage wheel looks like one of those decorative reproductions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship%27s_wheel

identification: W. Appelt soda water Codd-neck bottle, Nuriootpa, South Australia (chip to top)
viewing_check: Check the marble is still captive, the extent of the top chip, embossing clarity and glass colour; a chip to the lip hurts value for collectors.
searches_tried: WebSearch x3: W. Appelt Nuriootpa Codd bottle; Appelt Nuriootpa aerated water history; Appelt Codd sold price auction. Opened the Barossa Magazine article for history. Found GDL Auctions antique bottle catalogue PDFs but could not open them (host blocked from my shell), and Roycroft past-auction page not opened. No price recorded.
story: Appelt's was a soft drink and aerated water maker in the Barossa town of Nuriootpa, SA, described in a local history as a thriving rival of the older Warnecke cordial factory, which was sold about 1919 and wound up by 1922. Codd bottles sealed the fizz with a glass marble pushed up by gas pressure, patented by Hiram Codd in 1872. https://www.barossamag.com/?p=5165

identification: Tub of old bottles: a Leicester stoneware stone ginger beer bottle ('...& Sons, Stone Ginger Beer, Leicester'), two Watkins imitation raspberry/strawberry flavour bottles, stoneware jars and a number of old clear/aqua glass bottles and a small tin of marbles
viewing_check: Look at each embossed bottle for a maker or town name (especially any Tasmanian or Australian brewer/aerated-water firm), check for cracks and chips, and confirm the stoneware label wording.
searches_tried: WebSearch: Leicester stone ginger beer bottle '& Sons' (maker name not readable, nothing found); Watkins flavour bottle history (opened glassbottlemarks.com). No priced comparables found for a mixed tub, so no entries.
story: The Watkins flavour bottles come from the J. R. Watkins Company, founded in 1868 in Plainview, Minnesota (moved to Winona in 1885), a door-to-door seller of extracts, flavourings and remedies. The stoneware ginger beer bottle is an English example from Leicester; the maker's name is not legible enough in the photo to identify. https://glassbottlemarks.com/?p=1157

identification: Painted cast iron rooster (cockerel) weathervane with arrow and N-E-S-W directionals, modern decorative garden piece

entries.note: New flat-profile red rooster vane, not painted cast iron and a different design; shown only as the going price for a new Australian rooster vane.

viewing_check: Check whether it is really cast iron (heavy) or a lighter reproduction, the state of the paint and the spindle and mounting bracket.
searches_tried: WebSearch: painted cast iron rooster weathervane price Australia; weathercock history. Core Supply Group (Esschert cast iron rooster vane) page opened, wholesale, no price. Glenview listing read for asking price.
story: Roosters top weathervanes because, per a story repeated by weathervane sellers, Pope Nicholas I in the ninth century decreed every church should display a rooster as a reminder of Peter's betrayal; whether that is the true origin is often disputed. The Armitage vane looks like a modern decorative reproduction, not an old church or farm vane. https://www.glenviewproducts.com.au/shop/red-rooster-weather-vane/

identification: Three old irons: a Chinese brass charcoal 'pan' (silk) iron with wooden handle, a chrome/nickel electric iron with blue handle (likely 1920s-30s), and a cast-iron sad iron

entries.note: Vintage Chinese brass silk (coal) iron, wood handle with coins, 16in long, 6 bids; this is only the Chinese pan iron part of the Armitage lot, and an old US result. [AUD 26 converted at USD 1 = AUD 1.54]

viewing_check: Check for maker's marks on the electric iron (brand, voltage) and cord; look at the brass pan iron for dragon or other decorative work and coins on the handle, and for cracks in the cast-iron iron.
searches_tried: WebSearch x2: Chinese brass pan iron charcoal sold price; history of the sad iron/flat iron. Opened EBTH (SOLD US$17) and Wikipedia Clothes iron. Dealer asking pages for Chinese silk irons (eBay, Chairish) appeared in search but were not opened.
story: Before electricity, irons were solid cast lumps heated on a stove (sad irons) or hollow ones filled with burning charcoal like the Chinese pan iron; the electric flatiron was patented by American Henry W. Seely on 6 June 1882 and weighed nearly 15 pounds. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clothes_iron

identification: Framed Royal Australian Navy badge print, H 66 x W 43 cm (printed badge/crest; date and printer not confirmed)
viewing_check: Check the badge design: Tudor crown with left-handed rope and Federation Star points to 1949-57; St Edward's crown to 1957 on; plain oval rope to 1968 on. Check for printer or date marks in the margin and whether it is a print or a painted plaque.
searches_tried: WebSearch: Royal Australian Navy badge print framed vintage HMAS crest; RAN badge history crest print. Only museum records (Victorian Collections, AWM) and no priced comparable seen.
story: The RAN's official badge was only adopted on 23 August 1949, after a Hobart building surveyor asked for a naval symbol for the Hobart Cenotaph, so the badge has a Tasmanian origin. The design was altered in 1957 (St Edward's crown, right-handed rope) and in 1968 (plain oval rope, Federation Star and four dots removed), which lets you date a print by its details. Source: https://www.navy.gov.au/history/traditions/official-badge-design-history

identification: Vintage railway signal lamp, H 34 cm (kerosene railway lamp; railway, maker and type not yet identified from the catalogue line)
viewing_check: Look for stamped railway initials (TGR, VR, NSWGR etc.), maker marks, lens colours and whether the burner and font are present. Railway-marked examples are the collectable ones.
searches_tried: WebSearch: vintage railway signal lamp Australian railways kerosene lamp Tasmanian Government Railways; railway signal lamp sold auction Australia Beehive lamp Adlake. Fetched Noble Numismatics lot 426469 (pair of early 1900s signal lamps, estimate $30-40 range, realised $30, but the page gave no sale date so not recorded) and Museums Victoria 414524. No dated comparable recorded.
story: Kerosene hand and signal lamps like this were the everyday tools of Australian railway staff; Museums Victoria holds a Victorian Railways signalman's lamp with a rotating inner body that shows red, blue or clear light through the lens. Source: https://collections.museumsvictoria.com.au/items/414524

identification: German-made tinplate toy magic lantern projector, sold with vintage cameras (mixed lot)
viewing_check: Look for maker marks (Bing 'GBN', Ernst Plank, Carette, Falk) and an original chimney, lens and burner; check which cameras are in the lot, as a Kodak/Leica/folding camera may carry the value.
searches_tried: WebSearch: German magic lantern projector Plank/Bing/Lapierre sold; Bing Nuremberg magic lantern history; tinplate German magic lantern hammer price Australia. Theriault's, Leitz and Eron Johnson pages seen but gave no price text I could read, so no priced comparable recorded.
story: Tinplate toy magic lanterns were a Nuremberg speciality: Bing advertised lanterns from 1866 and by 1900 employed several thousand workers, while Ernst Plank made similar lanterns; Bing's marks changed to Bing Werke in 1930 and production wound up after 1931. Source: https://luikerwaal.com/merk_bing1_uk.htm

identification: Stoneware bottle in wicker (cane) casing, H 40 cm (large cane-cased jar/flagon, likely a spirit, vinegar or acid carrier; maker unmarked in catalogue)
viewing_check: Look for impressed or stamped maker or merchant marks on the shoulder or base (Doulton, Bourne, a Tasmanian or Melbourne wine merchant), and check the cane casing for breaks and the neck for chips.
searches_tried: WebSearch: stoneware bottle wicker casing demijohn antique; wicker covered stoneware bottle Australia sold Doulton OR Bourne Denby. Found only a museum record and decor demijohns (glass), no sold or asking price for a stoneware equivalent.
story: Cane-cased stoneware bottles like this are held by museums as everyday domestic and trade containers; the WA Museum has a very similar 32 cm cream stoneware bottle in a cane casing with a cane handle, donated 1995, with no maker or use recorded. Source: https://museum.wa.gov.au/online-collections/node/79029

identification: Cast iron coin bank (type, maker and whether original or reproduction not stated; photos not viewable)
viewing_check: Biggest question is original versus modern reproduction (many mechanical banks were copied, often in Asia). Check for casting marks (J&E Stevens, Kyser & Rex, Hubley, Arcade), screws vs original pins, paint wear and whether any mechanism works.
searches_tried: WebSearch: cast iron mechanical coin bank J&E Stevens/Kyser Rex/Hubley sold auction; cast iron money box coin bank vintage Australia auction sold hammer. Pages read gave only US high-end results (Morphy 14 Jan 2017) not comparable to an unidentified bank; no like-for-like price.
story: American cast iron mechanical banks by firms such as J&E Stevens and Kyser & Rex are a serious collecting field: at Morphy's 14 Jan 2017 sale a J&E Stevens 'Jonah and the Whale' made $119,925 with premium. Most ordinary or reproduction cast iron banks are worth a tiny fraction of that, so identification is everything. Source: https://www.antiquesandthearts.com/morphy-auctions-sells-peter-browns-mechanical-still-bank-collection-2
